name: OpenBMB/ChatDev
why: The CEO/CTO/programmer/reviewer/tester waterfall of T1, kept on the chatdev1.0 branch; main is now a zero-code workflow platform. Borrow the phase-and-role chat chain as a design to test, not its reliability (T7 reports 41% to 86.7% failure rates across seven open-source multi-agent systems incl. ChatDev and MetaGPT).

name: FoundationAgents/MetaGPT
why: SOP-encoded roles that hand each other structured documents (PRD, design) rather than chat (T2). Borrow: typed artifacts between roles and executable feedback; lesson: the repo's last push is Jan 2026 and the README's news is now about a hosted product (MGX), so treat it as a reference design.

name: OpenBMB/AgentVerse
why: Recruit-decide-execute-evaluate loop of T3 with Solo vs Group setups. Lesson from T3/T10: the group was not reliably better than one agent; stale since 2024-09 so read, do not depend.

name: microsoft/autogen
why: Archived and unmaintained (README says so); group-chat and conversation framework for multi-agent apps. Lesson: a popular framework can be abandoned, so the kit should not build on a third-party orchestration layer; license reads CC-BY-4.0 so check LICENSE files before any copying.

name: FSoft-AI4Code/AgileCoder
why: Sprint planning, backlog and review per sprint (T5): the agile alternative to ChatDev's waterfall. Borrow the backlog-plus-sprint-review structure to compare with a plain loop; stale since 2024-10.

name: multi-agent-systems-failure-taxonomy/MAST
why: Failure taxonomy (14 modes) plus 1,600+ annotated traces and an LLM-judge annotator (T7). Borrow the taxonomy as the checklist for auditing the kit's own traces; no repo license, so read the code only and take data from the Hugging Face dataset terms.

name: mahmoudsajjadi/pace
why: Reviewer checklist and accounting utilities for equal-budget comparisons of multi-agent against single-agent (T9). Borrow: the baseline ladder (greedy, sampled, budget-matched, Pareto) for the benchmark's no-team arm; brand new and 3 stars, so verify before relying on it.

name: anthropics/claudes-c-compiler
why: Working files of the 16-agent run in T16: current_tasks/ lock files, DESIGN_DOC.md, ideas/. Process to borrow: file-lock task claiming through git, a near-perfect task verifier, CI to stop regressions; its own README warns the code is unvalidated.

name: obra/superpowers
why: Spec, then plan, then subagent-driven development where agents work through each task while the work is inspected and reviewed (README claims hours-long autonomy). Process to borrow: spec sign-off before build and per-task review; the autonomy claim is unmeasured, so test it on the benchmark.

name: bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD
why: Agile role-based method (clarify, plan, build and verify, learn) with decisions kept explicit and context carried forward in written artifacts. Borrow the artifact handoffs; GitHub detects no license (README badge says MIT), so confirm the LICENSE file before copying.

name: SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent
why: About 100 lines of Python and a README claim of over 74% on SWE-bench Verified: the strong single-agent baseline to run at equal budget against the kit's team (T8, T9, H11). Lesson: minimal scaffolds nearly match heavy ones.

name: gastownhall/gastown
why: Mayor coordinator plus worker agents whose work state lives in git-backed hooks and a ledger rather than in agent memory. Borrow: durable handoff state that survives restarts; its claim of scaling to 20-30 agents is the README's own and unmeasured.

name: anthropics/claude-code-action
why: Runs Claude Code as a PR reviewer in CI on a fresh runner, so the reviewer starts without the builder's context, the pattern T17 says works best. Borrow it for the QA role's code review.

name: The-PR-Agent/pr-agent
why: Open-source PR reviewer (formerly qodo-ai/pr-agent). Use it as a reference review agent whose comments can be scored for signal against T13's 60.2% low-signal finding.

name: microsoft/Agensh
why: Orchestrator-free harness (shared Git workspace, message log, claim-and-verify loop) from T21; a model for coordination through files and git rather than a lead agent

name: JiayiGeng/CAID
why: Manager plus engineers in isolated git worktrees with test-gated merges (T20); no license, so read only and do not copy

name: cooperbench/CooperBench
why: CooperBench tasks and runner (T19): two-agent same-repo coding tasks with a Solo baseline, usable as a coordination stress test; no license, so read only

name: ybkim95/TeamBench
why: TeamBench (T18): Planner/Executor/Verifier with OS-enforced role separation and a Solo arm; a template for a role-separated, grader-anchored team benchmark

name: rm206/ParallACT_data_and_code
why: ParallACT data and code (T22, linked from the paper's project page): orchestrator-free parallel agents vs single-agent oracle and serial handoff; no license, so read only

name: few-sh/harden-v0
why: Hacker-fixer-solver loop that hardens outcome verifiers (T24); a pattern for stress-testing the kit's tester and benchmark graders
